name: REF192ESZ-REEL7
title: Precision micropower low-dropout voltage references, REF191 to REF198
summary: A family of series bandgap references with outputs of 2.048 V, 2.5 V, 3.0 V, 3.3 V, 4.096 V, 4.5 V and 5.0 V. Each needs only about 100 mV of headroom, draws under 45 µA, sources up to 30 mA and has an active-low SLEEP input that drops the supply current below 15 µA and leaves the output high impedance. The best (E) grade holds ±2 mV initial accuracy and 5 ppm/°C maximum drift; outputs are protected against shorts.
key_figures: 45 µA max; 15 µA max in sleep
up to 15 V operating; 18 V absolute maximum

notes: REF198GRUZ-REEL7 has an ordering quantity of 2,500; the other -REEL7 options are 1,000.

circuits.title: Ripple rejection test circuit
circuits.description: Ripple rejection fixture. A 15 V supply feeds VS through 1 kΩ; a signal generator couples ripple onto VS through 10 µF, and a second 10 µF from VS brings the input ripple out as REF for comparison. The output is loaded with 1 µF and 1 kΩ and AC-coupled to OUTPUT through 10 µF.

circuits.title: Output impedance test circuit
circuits.description: Output impedance fixture. VS is held at 7 V with 1 µF to ground and the output carries 1 µF. A 4 V DC source in series with a 2 V p-p generator drives the output node through a series resistor, and an impedance meter Z reads the output node against ground.

parts.note: impedance meter; pin 1 to the output, pin 2 to ground

notes: Misprint: the resistor value 200V should read 200 Ω.

circuits.title: Load transient response test circuit
circuits.description: Load step fixture: 15 V on VS, 1 µF on the output, and a current sink stepping the load between 0 and 10 mA.

circuits.title: Power-on response time test circuit
circuits.description: Turn-on fixture: a pulse generator steps VS to 7 V and the output, with 1 µF on it, is watched as it comes up.

circuits.title: SLEEP response time test circuit
circuits.description: Shutdown timing fixture: VS at 15 V, a pulse generator drives SLEEP, and the output carries 1 µF and a current-sink load.

circuits.title: Basic voltage reference connections
circuits.description: The standard hookup. VS is bypassed with 10 µF and 0.1 µF, the output with a 1 µF tantalum and 0.1 µF; pins 1, 5, 7 and 8 stay open. SLEEP is the shutdown input and goes to VS when shutdown is not needed.

circuits.title: Membrane switch controlled power supply
circuits.description: The reference used as a small low-dropout supply with push-button on and off. A 10 kΩ from SLEEP to the output keeps SLEEP low at power-up, so the output stays off. Pressing ON pulls SLEEP to VS through 1 kΩ; the output comes up and the internal pull-up then holds SLEEP high. Pressing OFF grounds SLEEP and the output shuts down.

circuits.title: Boosted 3.3 V reference with current limiting
circuits.description: A REF196 with a PNP pass transistor for loads to 150 mA at 3.3 V from a 6 V to 9 V supply. U1's own supply current flows through R1 and R2 and biases Q1, which carries most of the load current. Q2 senses the drop across R4 and clamps Q1's drive near 300 mA. U1's output is taken to the load point by a heavy sense conductor so the output is regulated at the load. Other REF19x parts set other outputs: REF192 2.5 V, REF193 3.0 V, REF194 4.5 V, REF195 5.0 V.

parts.note: anode to SLEEP, cathode to VC; fitted for shutdown control

notes: U1's OUTPUT is wired by a heavy conductor to the sense point S at the load, where Q1's collector joins at point F.
SLEEP is linked to Q2's collector at X. For shutdown control that link is cut and the CMOS source VC drives SLEEP through D1.

circuits.title: Negative precision reference without precision resistors
circuits.description: An integrator turns any REF19x into a negative reference. The reference output drives A1 through 1 kΩ, and A1 with its 1 µF feedback capacitor drives the reference's own GND pin through 100 Ω until the output pin sits at 0 V; the GND node is then −VREF. A 2N3906 and two 10 kΩ resistors keep the SLEEP function usable from TTL/CMOS logic.

parts.note: half of an OP295 or OP291

circuits.title: Stacking two references for summed outputs
circuits.description: Two references fed from one supply with U2's ground pin on U1's output, so VOUT1 is U1's voltage and VOUT2 is the sum of both. R1 gives U1 a minimum load to carry U2's ground current. With two REF192 the outputs are 2.5 V and 5.0 V; REF192/REF194 give 2.5 V and 7.0 V, REF192/REF195 2.5 V and 7.5 V. VS must exceed VOUT2 by at least 0.15 V.

circuits.title: Stacking a REF192 on an AD589
circuits.description: A REF192 stacked on a 1.235 V two-terminal reference. R1, across the REF192, biases the AD589 at about 500 µA, giving 1.235 V at VOUT1 and 3.735 V at VOUT2; VOUT1 can supply up to 450 µA. VS must exceed VOUT2 by at least 0.15 V.

circuits.title: Low dropout precision current source
circuits.description: A floating current source into a grounded load. The reference voltage sits across RSET (R1 plus trimmer P1), so the current into the load is VOUT/RSET plus the reference's own supply current. Example with a REF195: R1 = 953 Ω and a 100 Ω ten-turn P1 set 5 mA.

parts.note: ten-turn trimmer, pins 1 and 2 ends, W wiper

circuits.title: Switched 5 V / 3.3 V output reference
circuits.description: Two references with their outputs joined, one on and one asleep, chosen by a logic input. VC high turns U1 (REF195) on and U2 (REF196) off for 5.0 V; VC low gives 3.3 V. Two inverters of a 74HC04 make the opposite SLEEP drives. A REF194/REF195 pair gives 4.5 V and 5.0 V the same way. The two parts share C1 and C2.

circuits.title: Low dropout Kelvin-connected reference
circuits.description: A follower op amp buffers the reference and closes its loop at the load: its output drives the load through the force wire and its inverting input reads the load through the sense wire, so the drop in the wiring resistance RLW is removed. A1 can be half an OP295, half an OP292, or an OP183.

parts.note: half of an OP295 or OP292, or an OP183

notes: Sense and force join at the load.

circuits.title: Fail-safe 5 V reference
circuits.description: Two REF195 with joined outputs keep 5.000 V whether the main supply VS or a 6 V battery VBAT is present. U1 runs from VBAT, U2 from VS. AD820 U3 is a comparator with hysteresis (R3) that compares a share of VS from R1/R2 with a fixed 0.5 V taken from the output by R4/R5. With VS present U3 is high: U2 is on and Q1 pulls U1's SLEEP low, so the battery supplies only U1's standby current. When VS falls below about 5.5 V, U2 and Q1 turn off and U1 takes over; VS returns at about 6 V.

circuits.title: Low power strain gage circuit
circuits.description: A REF195 supplies a quad OP492 and sets the excitation current of the strain gage bridge. One amplifier with a 2N2222 forms a current sink: it holds a fixed fraction of the 5 V (set by 57 kΩ and 10 kΩ) across a 500 Ω 0.1% resistor, and the transistor draws that current through the bridge. The bridge top is fed from VIN through 100 Ω with 10 µF to ground. The other three amplifiers form an instrumentation amplifier: two input followers with gain set by 10 kΩ, 2.21 kΩ and 10 kΩ, and a difference stage of 20 kΩ resistors with 0.01 µF across its feedback.

parts.note: quad op amp; pins 4 and 11 are its supply

notes: Misprint: pin 13 of the OP492 is drawn unwired; it should join the upper 10 kΩ and the 2.21 kΩ.

equations.name: Stacked output
equations.expr: VOUT2 = VO(U1) + VO(U2); VS > VOUT2 + 0.15 V

operation.text: Seven fixed outputs (REF191 2.048 V to REF195 5.00 V, Table 1), each a bandgap reference with curvature-corrected drift and laser-trimmed thin-film resistors. Grades E, F and G set the initial accuracy and drift. Every grade comes in the 8-lead SOIC; PDIP and TSSOP come only in the lowest grade.
Runs from as little as about 100 mV above its output, up to 15 V, drawing under 45 µA. Sources up to 30 mA. Specified from −40°C to +85°C, with typical figures out to +125°C.
Pins 1 and 5 are where each part's output is trimmed by Zener zapping at the factory. Their resistance differs from pin to pin and from part to part, so nothing outside connects to them.
A short from the output to GND or to VS does no damage: the part shuts down and its supply current is limited to 40 mA.

Full load current is available with inputs from 3.3 V to 15 V. At high input voltage and load, check the dissipation against the package thermal resistance so the junction temperature limit is not passed.

A capacitor from OUTPUT to GND is required. The part is stable with more than 100 µF, and 1 µF gives the rated performance; 0.1 µF ceramic in parallel improves load transients. For line transients the input takes 10 µF electrolytic in parallel with 0.1 µF ceramic.

SLEEP is TTL/CMOS compatible and has an internal pull-up current source to VS, so an open-collector or open-drain driver can work it. A logic low or 0 V turns the output stage off; the output then goes high impedance and its voltage is set by whatever is connected to it. Sleep current is under 15 µA. Unused, SLEEP goes to VS (pin 2).
With tens of milliamps available, the reference can serve as a low-dropout supply in hand-held instruments, switched on and off through SLEEP.

In the boosted circuit Q1 has a gain of about 100 at 100 mA to 200 mA, so U1 never supplies more than a few mA, which keeps its drift low. Dropout rises by about 1.1 V from Q1's VBE and the drop across R4; with a REF196 the circuit still makes 3.3 V at 150 mA from a VS as low as 4.5 V. At VS = 5 V and a 300 mA limit, Q1 dissipates at most 1.5 W, inside a TO-220's 2 W; a smaller device such as a 2N4033 in TO-39 or TO-5 needs a lower limit, set by raising R4. C1 is tantalum for its low ESR and its larger value is needed for stability; C2 can be an ordinary electrolytic. With shutdown control fitted, start-up under heavy load is less clean and can take several milliseconds, 150 mA loads are still controlled, and large load capacitance is best avoided.

The integrator moves the reference's GND pin until its output pin is at 0 V, so the negative output equals the chosen part's voltage without matched resistors. Rail-to-rail amplifiers suit the circuit but need some millivolts of headroom when they deliver load current, which affects the choice of negative supply.

The lower reference must sink U2's bias current (50 µA to 100 µA) and also the base drive of U2's PNP output device, through its own load or R1. When U1's minimum load is not known, R1 is chosen to pass about 600 µA with VOUT1 across it. Each reference keeps its own input and output bypass capacitors, and either one can deliver its full rated DC current. The lowest VS is VOUT2 plus U2's dropout. With a two-terminal reference such as the AD589, its minimum and maximum current must be respected.
Accuracy holds for currents from the reference's own supply current (30 µA typical) to about 30 mA. The low dropout leaves the most compliance voltage for the load.

A part in sleep looks like an open circuit at its output and draws at most 15 µA from its supply. A part that is on sources up to its rating but can sink only a few µA, the current of its internal output divider. Outputs can therefore be joined and the output follows whichever part is on. Rising transitions are fast; falling ones wait for the load RL to discharge the output capacitor (1 µF typical), several milliseconds for 100 Ω to 1 kΩ. Settling to ½ LSB at 10 bits takes more than 7.6 time constants.

Narrow traces are about 0.45 mΩ per square in 1 oz copper, so load current through them makes an ILOAD × RWIRE error. An op amp that senses at the load and forces through the supply trace removes it; the OP295, OP292 and OP183 suit this.

With the R1 to R3 values shown, VS switches over at about 5.5 V falling and 6 V rising. The thresholds can be changed for other supplies, and other REF19x parts from 2.5 V to 5 V can serve as U1 and U2. The AD820 works down to a 3.3 V supply and swings within a few mV of its rails. All the switching circuit runs from VS, so with VS gone the output comes from U1.
Low-voltage amplifiers such as the OP492 or OP747 suit the circuit. Other REF19x parts fit with changed component values, and the whole circuit can be switched on and off through SLEEP.
